sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year, from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145].
Operating income grew faster, at a 9.9% CAGR [F146], but net income compounded at only 0.4% [F147].
Revenue rose 22.3% in FY2022 [D131] as fuel cost recovery revenues increased about $1,716 million on higher fuel and energy prices [P51].
Operating margin fell 14.6pp in FY2021 [D107] and rose 23.5pp in FY2023 [D177]; the filings cited do not explain either swing.
FPL is the dominant driver, at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], down from 76.5% in FY2020 [D258].
FPL added 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025 [D273][D236].
FPL operating revenues rose $1,243 million, primarily on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues [P21].
Operating income grew 10.7% in FY2025 [D237], with an incremental operating margin of 34.8% [D256] against an operating margin of 32.1% [F24].
Diluted shares rose 0.6% in FY2025 [D251] while net income fell 1.6% [D238], so diluted EPS fell 2.1% [D240].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sits above the window median of 30.3% [D300] and the peer median of 25.7% [D311], but below the 41.3% high [D299].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue from 23.2% [D224][D189], as D&A increased $951 million, mainly on about $1,090 million of deferred storm cost amortization [P16].
The pack holds no cost-line bridge for the 23.5pp FY2023 margin move [D177], so its drivers are not explained here.
Net margin was 26.5% [F40], 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin [F24], as other expense reached $3,750 million [X64].
Corporate and Other results fell $1,256 million, mainly on about $1,002 million of unfavorable after-tax non-qualifying hedge impacts [P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion in FY2025 [F64] was 1.83x net income [D227], against 1.91x in FY2024 [D192].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% [D241], and its share of revenue slipped to 48.4% from 56.4% [D225][D190].
The shift from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses impacted FPL operating cash flow by about $89 million, mainly on higher fuel prices [P19].
Investing outflow of $23.9 billion [F72] was $11.4 billion above operating cash flow [F64]; the pack has no capex line, so free cash flow is not shown.
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025 from $80.6 billion in FY2024 [D231][D196], on total debt of $95.0 billion [D230].
Net cash was -357.4% of revenue [D232], the 0th percentile among four utilities peers, whose median is -228.4% [D314][D315].
Debt issued of $23.4 billion [X90] was more than twice debt repaid of $10.3 billion [X98], while buybacks plus dividends were $4.68 billion [D233].
Return on average equity of 13.1% [D235] ranks in the 100th percentile of four peers, above their 11.6% median [D316][D317].
Net debt rose every year to $92.2 billion in FY2025 from $34.3 billion in FY2018 [R2][D231][D9], and higher average debt balances weighed on Corporate and Other results [P8].
The effective tax rate was -17.7% in FY2025 against 5.6% in FY2024 [R4][D226][D191], reflecting higher clean energy tax credits [P11][P15].
Equity method impairments tied to XPLR were about $0.7 billion in 2025 and $0.8 billion in 2024 [P12], and non-qualifying hedges add earnings volatility [P6].
The current ratio of 0.60x in FY2025 is below 1.0x [R1][F128], though it is the highest reading in the window [D305].
I dropped the FY2024 revenue decline of 5.2% [R3][D201] as benign: lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel recovery of $526 million explain it [P34].
Operating margin holding above the window median of 30.3% [D300] would confirm the FY2025 level of 32.1% [F24]; a reading below it would reverse that, in the FY2026 10-K.
Net cash worse than -357.4% of revenue [D232] would extend the debt build described above, in the FY2026 10-K.
An effective tax rate above the FY2024 level of 5.6% [D191], versus -17.7% in FY2025 [D226], would signal less credit support for net income, in the FY2026 10-K.
